to make a wish upon a star

by moondrinker

Summary

The golden star was getting awfully closer. And bigger. It really was pretty, Phainon thought, still staring right at it. His eyes burned but he kept looking anyways. 

…Was it supposed to be coming directly towards him? 

Too late. The sky lit up a brilliant gold and Phainon ducked his head, yelping. A loud boom! echoed through the forest and the ground shock heavily. The birds cawed angrily, and a hoard of wildlife came running away from the direction where the star fell. 

"What the fuck," Phainon whispered. "That was so cool." 

A voice that sounded suspiciously like Cyrene cried out, Don't go looking towards the direction of the loud and scary noise! 

Another voice that sounded like Phainon himself said, Wow! Let's go looking for that star! 

Phainon went looking for the star. 

Or: Mydei is the star that crash lands onto Aedes Elysiae. He is rescued by a boy named Phainon.

Written for Phaidei Week Day 4: Mythology

chapters.title: to make a wish upon a star
chapters.html:
Legends said that if you wished upon a star, your dreams would come true. They did not mention the price needed to pay to grant the wish, nor how the stars came into possession of that ability. 

It was true, however, that stars could grant wishes. But they were picky. Cold and solemn. Wishes were not meant to be thrown away, like how humans threw away their gold. 

There was a way to coerce a star into granting wishes, but such methods could only be accessed by either the purest or cruelest of hearts. And no star wanted to be held captive by the whims of a human. So they hid away in the sky, locking away their gifts. 

The humans could suffer. There was no need to interfere. 

When their youngest — little Mydeimos — expressed an interest in humans, many warned him to stay away. Humans were not worth throwing away their comfortable life. Only his mother, the fair Lady Gorgo, humored her son. 

"Mydeimos, my blessing," she said, nuzzling into her child's soft cheeks. "What is your wish?" 

"Silly mama!" the star laughed. "Stars can't grant other stars wishes!" 

"But you are more than just a star. You are my son." 

Mydeimos's eyes lit up. He smiled, then whispered, "Can I tell you a secret?" When Gorgo nodded, he leaned in closer. "I want… to wander through the years, or to become a beacon of light in the sky." 

Stars were meant to be free. They were meant to love with all of their hearts, and burn away with their passion at the end of their life. But fear had kept all of them chained in a gilded cage. Gorgo was old enough to remember the days of soaring through the skies. Stars could not wish, but she wished for her son to have that same freedom. 

"Then go," Gorgo said. Mydeimos turned to her, surprised. "Live. Be free. And when you find someone you love with all of your heart, enough to burn away your divinity, turn to the skies and tell your mama all about them. I will bless you, my sweet child." 

"Cyrene, look!" Phainon pointed at the night sky. Normally, nights in Aedes Elysiae were pitch dark — everyone had already retired for bed — but today, the skies were lit up. "It's a meteor shower!" 

"Wow!" Cyrene gasped. They had been playing with the mems, and were rushing home after losing track of time. "It's so pretty!" 

They glanced at each other. "Wellll," Phainon drawled out. "We're already in trouble, so it's not like we can get yelled at more." 

Cyrene whacked the back of his head. "Mom and Dad are going to ground us," she scolded, but her eyes had a mischievous glint to them. "Okay, fine. We can stay a little longer. But we have to be back before the sun starts to rise!" 

"Sure," Phainon said, fully planning on disobeying her. The mems would protect them if anything were to happen. But he was so enthralled by the stars, he didn't want to miss any moment of it. 

They eventually settled in an open clearing to watch the sky. Both children were mesmerized by the sight, completely forgetting that they had parents waiting for them at home. Eventually, Cyrene let out a loud yawn. 

"You go home first," Phainon said absentmindedly. "I'll follow you after." His eyes were glued to a particularly golden shooting star. It was brighter than the rest, and a pretty crimson streak trailed after its path. 

Cyrene must have been exhausted, because she left without arguing for once. Phainon shuffled around until he got more comfortable, still staring at the sky. He frowned. Hm…

The golden star was getting awfully closer. And bigger. It really was pretty, Phainon thought, still staring right at it. His eyes burned but he kept looking anyways. 

…Was it supposed to be coming directly towards him? 

Too late. The sky lit up a brilliant gold and Phainon ducked his head, yelping. A loud boom! echoed through the forest and the ground shock heavily. The birds cawed angrily, and a hoard of wildlife came running away from the direction where the star fell. 

"What the fuck," Phainon whispered. "That was so cool." 

A voice that sounded suspiciously like Cyrene cried out, Don't go looking towards the direction of the loud and scary noise! 

Another voice that sounded like Phainon himself said, Wow! Let's go looking for that star! 

Phainon went looking for the star. 

As it turned out, flying through the sky required a lot of precision and control. Control that Mydeimos did not have. He went tumbling through the sky, crashing and bumping into other bits of rocks. 

"Ow!" 

The rocks did not respond to him. Rude. 

Mydeimos's eyes caught an area on the planet below him. It was gorgeous — all golden wheat fields, colorful flowers, the picture of happiness and peace. He squinted. Everyone should have been asleep, but there was a boy watching him. The boy had the most brilliant blue eyes Mydeimos had ever seen. He instinctively started veering towards the boy. 

"Oh, wait! No!" 

He couldn't catch his balance again. A flash of white blinded him, and he squeezed his eyes shut right before hitting the ground. 

Boom! 

"Ouch…" Mydeimos groaned. He had crash landed into a crater. Or perhaps it was more accurate to say that he made the crater. "Oh, Mama is going to be so mad at me." He slumped backwards, too tired to even think about ascending again. 

"Hello?" A voice said above him. Mydeimos opened his eyes. The boy with the pretty eyes was here! And he had the most peculiar white hair, as well. Mydeimos was so busy staring at him, he missed what the boy was saying. "Err… hello? Are you okay? Can you understand me?" 

Oops. "I'm okay!" Mydeimos said. He stood up and tried to jump out of the crater. It was too tall. "Can you help me out?" 

After a bit of a struggle, the boy finally was able to grab his hand and pull with a surprising amount of strength. Mydeimos came toppling over the edge of the crater, face planting into the boy's chest. When he straightened, the boy was staring at him wide-eyed, face completely red. He giggled a bit. Humans were amusing! 

"Thank you for your help." 

"Uh," the boy said, still staring at him. "Uh, what?" 

Mydeimos frowned. Could the boy not understand him? They were communicating just moments before. "My name is Mydeimos. What is your name?" 

"My..mos?"

"No, no. My-dei-mos." 

The boy frowned. "Me-di-mos." 

Mydeimos sighed. "You can just call me Mydei." 

His brilliant blue eyes lit up. "I'm Phainon! It's nice to meet you! Are you a star?" 

Phainon. What a weird name. And he couldn't pronounce Mydeimos? Wait a minute. "I'm not a star," Mydei blurted out. 

Phainon nodded at him solemnly. "Uh huh. And I'm not a human." 

"I'm not!" 

"Rightttt," Phainon drawled out. Mydei took back everything he had said about this boy. He had never met anyone as infuriating as Phainon. "Then why are you glowing like that? And why do you look so pretty? You're the most beautiful person I've ever met!" 

Mydei looked down at himself. Oh. He was glowing faintly, a pretty crimson-gold. "I don't know how to stop glowing," he admitted. "And I can't change the way I look. This was how I was born." Or his human version of his star form, anyways. 

"Really?" Phainon said, surprised. "Wow! Do all stars look like you?" 

Mydei frowned. "I dunno. Do all humans look like you?" 

"Hmm." Phainon placed his hands under his chin, thinking. "But if you're a star, how come you're here?" 

There was no point in hiding it anymore. "I fell," Mydei admitted. He didn't mention why he had fallen. 

"Are you hurt?" Phainon asked, alarmed. "What about your parents? They must be worried about you!" 

"It's just my mom and I," Mydei said. "I should probably go back home, though." All of the stars had warned him not to make contact with humans. Phainon was a little silly though, so surely it was okay? He closed his eyes and concentrated. 

When he opened them again, Phainon was still there but sitting down and yawning. "Oh. I'm still here." 

"Huh. Maybe try jumping up and down?" 

What an absurd thought. Mydei gave a little hop anyways. Nothing happened. He was starting to get a bit concerned. 

"Aren't you a star?" Phainon pointed out. "Can't you just make a wish to like. Go back home?" 

"It doesn't work like that." Mydei rubbed his forehead. 

"Well, what if I wish for you to go back home?" 

That caught Mydei's attention. "Really? You would use your wish for that?" 

"Of course I would!" Phainon leaned in and grabbed his hand. "You deserve to go back home to your mom! My mama would miss me if I left…" His eyes grew watery. 

"But," Mydei hesitated. "If I left, I wouldn't be able to grant any of your wishes." Phainon was nothing like what the other stars had told him. He wasn't a power-hungry, wish-thieving human at all. 

"I don't care! If I wanted something, I would work for it myself! Wishes take away all the joy of the journey." 

"That seems silly." Mydei paused in thought. "But if you could wish for anything, right at this moment, what would you want?" He half-expected Phainon to say something like I want a lot of gold, or I want to rule a kingdom. 

Phainon squeezed his eyes shut, thinking. "Hm… I'm kinda hungry right now. I wish for a piece of cake!" 

A slice of cake appeared mid-air and dropped straight into Mydei's hands, complete with utensils and all. Phainon's jaw dropped. So did Mydei's. 

"That's it? That's all you want?" He said incredulously. 

Phainon snatched the cake out of his hands and started to eat it. "It's yummy," he admitted. "But the fun is ruined! The best part about eating a cake is making it!" 

"I don't know how to make a cake." 

Phainon beamed. "I'll teach you!" He paused. "I mean, only if you want! If you can't go home, you can stay with me. We'll give you a home until you gather your strength! But you need to do something about that glow. And your face. It's kinda distracting." 

"I can't do anything about my face," Mydei grumbled, but he closed his eyes once more. This time, the glow faded away. He opened his eyes. "I want to stay with you. Where are your housing quarters?" 

The sun was just starting to rise when Phainon and Mydei made their way back home. Hieronymus and Audata were sitting at the dining table, Cyrene across from them looking at Phainon guiltily. She must have told them where he was. 

"You." Hieronymus crossed his arms. "What were you thinking?" 

"Where have you been?" Audata demanded. 

Cyrene said, "Uh, Phainon. Who is that behind you?" 

Good change of subject, Cyrene! Phainon mentally praised her. He shoved Mydei in front of him. "Mom, Dad, this is Mydei! I found him in the forest. He lost his parents, so he's staying with us now!" Technically, nothing he said was a lie. 

Predictably, Audata's eyes softened. "Oh, how sad! Come here, Mydei. Are you hungry? Tired? Cold?" She ushered Mydei away, who looked back at Phainon helplessly. 

"What am I going to do with you?" Hieronymus muttered. He rubbed at his forehead. Phainon beamed winningly at him. "As long as you promise not to do that again." 

"I promise!" 

"Liar," Hieronymus said, but he was smiling. He ruffled Phainon's hair before heading to the kitchen to help with his wife. Cyrene whirled on him the moment he left. 

"Phainon!" she hissed. "Don't tell me he's the shooting star!" 

"Whaaat?" Phainon laughed nervously. "That's crazy! Stars aren't humans. Especially not one as pretty as Mydei." 

She glared at him. "You wouldn't lie to me, right?" 

"I would never," Phainon lied. 

Cyrene squinted suspiciously at him. "Ugh. You're so annoying." 

"Love you too, sis. Do you want some cake?" 

She jumped up in joy. "Yes!" 

As it turned out, teaching Mydei how to bake a cake required a lot of effort. Phainon was starting to regret his words and just command Mydei to summon a cake, but he couldn't. Mydei had looked so in awe when Phainon didn't want anything from him. Just how badly did people treat stars to make him act that way? 

The kitchen was covered in flour by the time they finished baking. Cyrene and Phainon crowded over Mydei as he pulled the cake out of the oven. He looked nervous. "How is it?" 

Phainon stuck his fork straight in the middle and bit into it. "Wow!" His eyes widened. "Mydei, it's really good! Even better than your first one!" 

"Really?" Cyrene leaned across from him and nabbed a piece. "It is! Good job, Mydei!" 

Mydei beamed. His golden eyes reflected the light, making them shine brighter than ever. Phainon felt the ridiculous urge to pinch his cheeks. But that was probably weird, so he did the next best thing: he grabbed a handful of flour and threw it straight in Mydei's face. 

Mydei shrieked and snatched the nearby pitcher of water to dump it on Phainon. Not to be outdone, Cyrene tackled Phainon straight into the pile of messy ingredients. "Food fight!" 

"You," Audata seethed moments later, stepping into the destroyed kitchen. "Just what. Do you think. You're doing." 

She made Cyrene and Phainon clean up the kitchen by hand. Of course, Mydei was able to sit and eat his cake. No fair. 

Phainon playfully stuck his tongue out at Mydei, who wrinkled his nose at him. In the span of minutes, he had managed to almost eat all of their cake. Ugh. Maybe summoning food had its advantages after all. 

Cyrene leaned in closer to him, smiling. "We should take him to the Membrance Maze!" She whispered eagerly. Her earlier hesitation towards Mydei was long forgotten. "I think the mems will really like him." 

Phainon nodded. He wanted to take Mydei to see all the wonderful parts about Aedes Elysiae. Though the boy was a star (and wasn't that so cool?), the golden shine of his hair and eyes, as well as his soft smile, fit in nicely with the town. He wanted to wake up everyday and play with Mydei, to teach him how to farm, to skip class and go to the Membrance Maze together with Cyrene. Phainon's shoulders slumped a little. But what if his mama missed him and wanted her son back home? He couldn't possibly do that to her. 

Phainon was so lost in thought, he didn't notice Cyrene come up to him, holding hands with Mydei. "We're going!" She chirped at him. Phainon absentmindedly followed along. Maybe the mems would know what to do. 

The mems loved Mydei. They loved him so much that when he entered the Membrance Maze, they all surrounded him, completely forgetting about Cyrene and Phainon. 

"Wow," Phainon said. He wasn't jealous at all. "Where's my welcome back?" 

He was ignored. Phainon was starting to regret bringing Mydei here. Then, he really got a good look at what was going on and felt bad for thinking that. Mydei was giggling softly to himself, his face lit up with childlike wonder. The mems were all laughing and flying around him excitedly, hiding in his hair, touching his clothes, patting his cheeks. They were delighted in a different way than they acted around Phainon and Cyrene. It made sense. Mems were fairies, right? So they must have sensed that Mydei was a star and not a regular human. 

Well that, and the fact that Mydei seemed to be enjoying himself so much, he had lost control of his powers and was glowing a faint golden sheen. Hopefully Cyrene didn't look too closely at him. 

Finally, some of the mems flew back to pamper Cyrene and Phainon. 

"A gift!" One of them chirped. "We must prepare a gift! Thank you, Phai-mem, Cyrene-mem! Thank you for bringing this lovely star!" 

They flew off into the garden. Moments later, they reemerged holding a flower crown. Mydei's eyes widened when he saw it. "Wow," he breathed. "Is that really for me?" 

"Of course!" Cyrene giggled. "It means they really like you!" 

Mydei gently took the crown and placed it on top of his head gingerly, like it was a coronation and not just a gift from the mems. "Thank you," he told them solemnly. "I'll never forget this gift." 

"So cute! So cute! Little Star Mem is so cute!" The mems chittered. 

Phainon found a seat at the base of a nearby tree, watching the scene unfold. He wanted to stay like his forever. He wanted Mydei to always smile like that. "If I had a wish…" Phainon murmured to himself, half asleep. "I would wish… for everyday to be just as peaceful as today." He slumped sideways, passed out from exhaustion. 

Cyrene and Mydei exchanged glances before giggling quietly. "Shh!" Cyrene whispered, placing a finger to her lips. "I told Phainon not to stay up all night, but he didn't listen to me," she teased. 

Mydei looked at her guiltily. "But it was my fault he was out so late." 

"Nah!" Cyrene smirked. "Come on, let's draw pictures on his face!" 

Cyrene had just finished placing a flower crown on his head when Phainon woke, blinking groggily. "Eh? What's going on?" He sat up. "Where's Mydei?" 

"Speaking with Dolimem." She winked at him. "I know Mydei's a star, by the way." 

Phainon winced. "Please don't be mad at me." 

"I'm not! I'm really proud of you. I know you just wanted to protect him. But we have to be more careful now. The mems told me that there are still some people who wish to harness the power of the stars."

Phainon's eyes widened. "Mydei seemed really surprised when all I wished for was cake last night," he admitted. 

Cyrene sat down next to him and patted his knee. "You're sweet," she said. "And Mydei… he's young. Innocent. Even if he's a star, he deserves the same childhood we have. So we have to make sure that all of his wishes come true — we'll be his own stars!" 

That sounded like a good idea. Out of earshot from them, Mydei was twirling in a circle with the mems, laughing when they all got dizzy and fell over. He caught Phainon's eye and waved happily. Phainon waved back. 

Cyrene rested her head on his shoulder. "I tried to divine his future while you were sleeping," she said softly. "I wasn't sure if it would work. The stars bless my divination, after all. But Phainon… I'm scared. I don't want Aedes Elysiae to suffer. I don't want us to suffer." 

Phainon patted her head. "It'll be okay," he said firmly. "I'll train and study hard to prepare for the future. And if anyone comes to take Mydei away, I'll fight them!" He believed it wholeheartedly. Nothing terrible had ever come to Aedes Elysiae. And if it did, he had his friends by his side. Cyrene was the strongest diviner in the whole world, and Mydei was a star! Who could possibly hurt them? 

Looking back on it, Phainon so desperately wished that he had savored that moment just a bit longer — that he had savored the sight of Mydei for a bit longer. 

The world was cruel, after all. And no one knew that better than the stars. 

Your majesty! We've finally located where the star's energy is coming from! It's in Aedes Elysiae, sir! 

Aedes Elysiae? …I see. Then I will lead my troops. Be prepared to take the star by all means necessary. Kill those who dare disobey me. 

Yes, sir! Long live the great King Eurypon! 

"3… 2… 1…" 

The light clicked open. 

"Happy birthday, Phainon!" 

Phainon rolled over in his bed and squinted against the light. Both Cyrene and Mydei were standing at his door. Mydei was holding a cake and Cyrene had on a makeshift party hat and party streamers. She beamed when she saw her brother looking at her. "Phainon!" she whisper-yelled. "Happy birthday!" 

Phainon groaned and smushed his face in the pillow. "I heard you the first time," he grumbled. They must have waited until midnight of his birthday to wake up him. Nevertheless, it was a sweet gesture. He sat up. "Thank you, really." 

Mydei didn't smile, but his eyes softened at the corners. "Don't be stupid. Of course we would make you a cake." 

After five years of living in the Phainon-Cyrene household, he had only grown taller and developed a bit of a dry humor. "Awww, Mydei," Phainon teased. "You really do care!" 

Cyrene was so excited, she was practically vibrating in her seat. "Okay, okay!" she said. "Can we eat now? I'm starving!" 

They dug into the cake, Phainon nearly moaning as he bit into the first bite. Mydei must have banned Cyrene from interfering — she liked to get too creative when baking. Also, the cake wasn't nearly as pink enough for her tastes. 

When they finished eating, they sat around Phainon's bed, idly chatting. Cyrene took out her tarot cards, randomly shuffling them. She had started doing that more often as a nervous habit. Phainon had no knowledge of divination, but he hoped Cyrene was okay. 

She must have noticed him staring, because she smiled reassuringly at him. "You're fifteen now, Phainon! One more year closer to being an adult!" 

"You're old," Mydei said flatly. Despite being a star, he had continued to age as a human would. A couple years ago, they had done the math to figure out how old Mydei was. The closest they could get was one year younger than Phainon — a fact the white-haired boy rubbed in his face often. Mydei got his revenge by calling Phainon an old hag any chance he got. 

Cyrene nudged him with her foot. "Don't say that! If he's old, then what am I?" 

"Ancient." 

"Practically pre-historic." 

Phainon and Mydei said at the same time. She playfully glared at them. "Ugh, you two are awful. I'm going to sleep." 

When the door clicked behind her, Phainon turned to Mydei, widening his eyes dramatically. Mydei made a face. "No. I'm tired. Go away." 

"Pleaseeee?" He pouted. 

Mydei grumbled as always, but he took his hand and let Phainon quietly lead them out of the house, into the forest, and past the Membrance Maze into a large clearing. The crater that Mydei had made was still there. Phainon laughed lightly. "I can't believe it's still there after five years." He traced the edge of it. Little Mydei had been too small to get out without help, but now it was practically tiny to them. 

"Well, it is a crater. It's not like it can just magically go away." Mydei sat down next to him and closed his eyes. Seconds later, a faint glow shone from his body. He sighed. "Looks like I still can't go home." 

Phainon frowned. "You would really leave on my birthday?" He tried to tell himself that he wasn't disappointed. It was just — he would be lonely! On his birthday of all days!" 

"No, silly. I like it here. I wanted to tell my mother that I was okay. But I think she knows anyways." 

Phainon scooted closer to Mydei, lacing their fingers together. After a brief pause, Mydei rested his head on Phainon's shoulder. His golden-crimson hair tickled Phainon's nose. He was so warm. Phainon sighed, delighted. He secretly hoped that Mydei's mom would let her son stay here forever. 

"Has your wish changed at all?" Mydei asked him. Both Cyrene and Phainon had forbid him from granting any wishes. It didn't matter if it was just for test answers or some extra coins when they accidentally forgot their wallets — Mydei was banned. 

"I don't have any wishes," Phainon smiled teasingly. "Actually hmm… I would really like some cake right now!" 

Mydei looked appalled. "We just ate cake!" The moment he said that, a slice of cake appeared and dropped into Phainon's lap. This was their tradition and their little secret — a slice of cake for Phainon's birthday. What Cyrene didn't know wouldn't hurt her. Plus, he liked seeing the way Mydei looked whenever Phainon asked him for something. His eyes would lit up and a soft smile would grace his face. Whenever he glowed, he looked like a divine being — like a star. 

Phainon wasn't blind. The boys in his class were getting older, and often spoke… differently about the other girls. Phainon had no interest in them, but he secretly thought Mydei was the most beautiful person he had ever seen. He had only grown more beautiful as the years passed — his features filled out more, he got taller, more comfortable in his body. 

I wish to kiss Mydei. Phainon's face flushed red. But he couldn't do that. It would be unfair for Mydei. He was happy just sharing these small moments with him. And maybe if his mom came to find him, he could ask for her permission to court her son. 

Yeah. That seemed like a good plan. 

Hours passed, and Phainon and Mydei were still talking about anything and everything. Well, more like Phainon was talking and Mydei was going "okay", "huh", or the occasional "interesting." The sun was already up when they were interrupted by a high-pitched voice. 

"Phai-mem! Little Star!" 

"Dolimem?" Phainon asked, shocked. He had never seen Dolimem leave the Membrance Maze before. "What's wrong? What happened?" 

"Evil people!" Dolimem squeaked out. "They have come for you, Little Star Mem! You must hide!" 

Phainon and Mydei both shot to their feet. "No," Phainon gasped out. He turned to Mydei, who had gone so pale, it only made his golden glow more noticeable. "Mydei, we have to go!" 

"Who is it?" Mydei demanded. "What have they done?" 

Dolimem stammered. "Please, Little Star, do not argue!" 

"What do they want?" Mydei snapped. 

Dolimem wailed out, "Cyrene-mem! They have Cyrene-mem captive!" 

Phainon's blood went cold. Cyrene. No. How could they know?

But it made sense. If you wanted to know where a star was hiding, you would target the girl whose abilities communicated with the stars. 

"I'm going." Mydei turned to Phainon. His eyes glowed a furious golden. "Don't you dare stop me." 

Phainon snatched his hand. "I'm coming with you!" 

They made their way back to Aedes Elysiae in record time. Dolimem was right — a group of soldiers were crowded around in a circle. In the middle of it was Cyrene, held at sword point by someone wearing a crown. Phainon blanched. He knew that royal crest. What was the mad King Eurypon doing here? 

Cyrene caught his eye and shook her head slightly. "Run," she mouthed, and winced as Eurypon dug his sword closer to her neck.

Eurypon sighed, bored. "No one will tell me?" He asked lazily. "Or will I have to kill everyone in this village before it comes out? I know it's here. We've been monitoring its powers." 

The crowd started to nervously murmur. 

"We don't know where the star is!" 

"Yeah! Let Cyrene go!" 

A man standing behind Eurypon raised an eyebrow. "Really? So in the past five years, there has been no one suspicious here? No one that suddenly appeared? No weird light or animal behavior from the forest?" 

Everyone went silent. Aedes Elysiae was small. Everyone knew each other. And everyone had kept quiet when Phainon paraded Mydei around five years ago, saying he was a friend. 

Mydei broke free from Phainon's hold and burst into the circle. "Stop it!" he shouted. "It's me! Let her go!" 

"Mydei!" Phainon yelled, furious. He tried to make his way forward but was cut off by the palace guards. 

Mydei clenched his fists tight and glared at Eurypon. "What do you want?" he snapped. 

Eurypon laughed. "Do you really expect me to believe this? You're just a child. Prove it." 

A bead of blood dripped down Cyrene's neck. She whimpered. "Mydei, no." 

Mydei licked his lips. "What do you wish for?" 

"Gold," Eurypon said instantly. He smiled cruelly. "And don't even think about answering another wish, like 'I wish for the king to drop dead.' I'll have this girl's head cut off before you can even think about it." 

Phainon pushed back the guards and ran to Mydei. "Mydei," he begged. "Don't." 

Mydei shoved him away. A burst of bright light, and a bag of gold coins appeared in his hands. Eurypon's eyes widened. He started to laugh hysterically. 

"What a fascinating little star," he said. It didn't sound as comforting as when the mems called Mydei "Little Star." "Do we have a deal? Come with me, and I will spare this village. At least until it is the last one standing." 

Mydei took a shuddering breath. "Stars don't deal in contracts," he snapped. "I'm not stupid. I can sense what weapons you have. I don't know how you did it, but you have some that can hurt me. You're not going to honor your word." 

"How clever." Eurypon curled his lip. "But I can promise you this: your village will be safe until we arrive back in Castrum Kremnos." 

"Mydei—" 

Mydei turned to face Phainon. "I'm sorry, Phainon," he said. "Thank you for taking me in these last five years. I had a lot of fun." 

No.

"I wish—" Phainon started to say. 

Mydei grabbed his chin and pressed his lips to his. Whatever Phainon was going to say vanished and he curled his hand around the back of Mydei's head, pulling him in closer. He felt like he was on fire. A tingling sensation traveled down his back, and when they pulled apart, Phainon felt as though he was seeing stars. Not metaphorically — but actual stars, staring at him in judgment. He blinked, and the world realigned. 

He licked his lips. "Mydei, please." 

"When we see each other again," Mydei blurted out. He looked panicked. "You can tell me your wish, okay?" 

"How sweet," Eurypon drawled out. "Come now. There isn't much time to waste." 

Phainon watched, horrified, as the guards stepped forward and forced heavy chains onto his wrists. Mydei turned back only briefly to look at Phainon. His eyes were dim. 

Yet he still left Aedes Elysiae with his head held high. 

When they arrived in Castrum Kremnos, Mydei was thrown into a large golden cage. He sneered. They just had to model it like a birdcage, didn't they? 

He didn't know how, but Eurypon had gotten his hands on a material that directly targeted the souls of stars. Even if he wanted to escape, he couldn't. And he couldn't grant wishes freely like this. 

Well. Not unless Phainon was here. Mydei pressed the tips of his fingers to his lips. He didn't regret that action one bit, even if he hadn't known until after. He narrowed his eyes at Eurypon, who was seated outside the cage. 

"What do you want?" 

Eurypon didn't hesitate. "What are the constraints of your ability?" 

The chains around his hands pulsed once, sending sharp waves of pain throughout his body. Mydei gritted his teeth. He refused to show weakness in front of Eurypon. "I cannot bend the rules of this world," he forced out. "If you wished for complete world domination, I cannot grant that right away." 

Eurypon looked intrigued. "What if I wished to take over a kingdom? How would that happen?" 

Mydei kept his mouth shut. Another wave of pain forced him to his knees. "I can do that for you. But you will still need to fight." 

"So it's like increased luck," Eurypon mused. "I can work with that. As for the gold? Summoning items out of thin air doesn't seem to comply with the rules of this world." 

"It comes from somewhere," Mydei said. "Not necessarily from your world. I am not making it from scratch. But get too greedy, and you'll ruin Castrum Kremnos's economy." 

"But you can summon weapons." 

"…Yes." 

Eurypon smiled. "I think that will be all," he said. "I hope you're comfortable, Little Star. You won't be leaving this cage for a very long time." 

Months passed, and Aedes Elysiae was no longer the peaceful, idyllic village it once was. Instead, the villagers prepared for war, in case Castrum Kremnos came at their doorstep. 

But it never did. Castrum Kremnos spread out their forces to attack other countries, but never Aedes Elysiae. Perhaps, the villagers murmured. The King was telling the truth after all. 

Cyrene shook her head at those rumors. "Look," she said. She led them to the borders of the wheat fields. There was a thin golden field surrounding them, stretched out until they couldn't see any further. "Mydei is still protecting us." 

Phainon took a deep breath. It still hurt him whenever Mydei was brought up. Even his parents tiptoed around him, despite being just as sad as him. They had loved Mydei like he was their son. 

Two years had almost passed when Phainon couldn't take it anymore. He stopped by the temple Cyrene prayed at and waited. At last, she saw him. 

"You're going." It wasn't a question. 

"Yes," Phainon said. "It was my fault he was caught. You told us not to let him grant any wishes, but I stupidly didn't think about why." 

"It wasn't just about that," Cyrene told him. "I wanted him to be a normal child. Children aren't slaves to other people's wishes." She sighed. "The stars haven't been responding to my questions. But I believe that if you go, he will protect you." 

"Will you…" he hesitated. "Will you come with me?" 

She smiled sympathetically at him. "I can't. Aedes Elysiae needs me, especially if you're leaving. But I can guarantee that you won't be alone. Go to Okhema first. Seek out Lady Aglaea — she will help you."

Okhema was one of the last standing countries. Its defense was strong enough that Castrum Kremnos hadn't bothered to attack it — mostly thanks to Lady Aglaea and her golden threads. Phainon nodded. Even if Lady Aglaea said no, he was still determined to rescue Mydei. 

Okhema was bright and noisy in a way Phainon had never experienced before. He took one step into the country, got cat-called by some passing strangers, and wondered if he could rescue Mydei by himself. 

Probably not. 

In any case, he had to at least keep his promise to Cyrene. Hopefully Lady Aglaea would have some advice for him, at the very least. 

People in Okhema were busy. They hustled around like they were getting paid for every minute they were spent working. Phainon tried to greet some passing strangers like he would at home, only to get stared at like he was gum on the bottom of their shoes. 

…He really did not like Okhema. 

He sat down at a nearby bench, overwhelmed. Cyrene had told him that Kephale's Dawn Device lit up the sky all day. It would be weird not to see the stars for once. Phainon's shoulders slumped down further. There was no point in seeing the stars if his star wasn't with him. 

"Wow," a sharp voice said behind him. "Today really isn't your day, isn't it?" They came to stand in front of him. The person who spoke was a woman of around average height, with gray hair, sharp eyes, and strangely, a feline like vibe to her — complete with a tail and all. Phainon must have been staring for too long, because she said, "You must be new to Okhema if this surprises you." 

He blinked. "How did you know I'm not from Okhema?" 

She raised and eyebrow and motioned to his clothing, for some reason. "Uh, because you're dressed like a wannabe highlighter? I would've definitely noticed you before. Anyways, what brings you here?" 

He perked up. Maybe she could help him? "Do you happen to know Lady Aglaea?" 

"Agy?" the woman said. "Of course I know Agy! Who doesn't? Oo-oo, are you in trouble? Are you going to be executed?" 

"What? No! Of course not!" 

"Hm, are you sure? You haven't done anything bad like, say, angered the king of Castrum Kremnos or painted a target on Okhema's back, right?" 

"Uh," Phainon said. He'd probably angered Eurypon when he hid Mydei from him, but that was over two years ago. But if Aglaea agreed to help him steal Mydei back, then Eurypon was definitely going to attack Okhema. "If I say no, will she help me?" 

The woman wagged her finger at him. "She can tell if you're lying! Wanna know how?" 

Phainon knew nothing about Lady Aglaea, so it was best to hear her out. "How?" 

She leaned in closer. "Did you know they say that the reflection of a sword shows a warrior's true heart? Take your sword out. I'll show you." 

Phainon had never heard of such a thing, so he handed the woman his sword and watched her. If Lady Aglaea was able to tell if he was lying, he wanted to cover all of his bases. 

The woman cackled at him. "Wow, you really are gullible, huh? Thanks for the nice sword. See ya!" She turned and sprinted off. Phainon stared at her. 

Wait a fucking minute. 

"Hey! Come back here!" He took off, chasing after her. How on Amphoreus was she so fast? Was she actually a cat? 

They must have been running for a solid five minutes before Phainon rounded a corner viciously. He reached out, expecting to grab her shoulder when— 

Crash! 

"Oh! Little Ica, are you okay?" 

Phainon groaned, feeling as though he just ran full speed at a wall. Soft hands propped him up. "Oh my goodness! Here, drink this." A water bottle was shoved into his hands. 

When Phainon opened his eyes, he wondered if he had died and went to the afterlife. Staring straight at him with beady little eyes was a really fat and pink… unicorn? 

"What the fuck?" he muttered to himself. 

An equally pink girl popped into view. "Hello? Can you hear me? Are you alright? Little Ica and I are really sorry!" She looked so guilty, Phainon couldn't help but feel ashamed for running like a maniac in a public area. 

He gave her a shaky smile. "I'm alright, miss. Is your… unicorn okay?" 

"My name is Hyacine! And this is Little Ica!" the woman said. Thankfully she seemed a lot nicer than the first girl. "Little Ica is a Pegasus, so he's alright! It takes a lot more than a fall to get him hurt." 

Little (?) Ica doot dooted at him and weirdly started to nudge at his pockets. Hyacine's face flushed bright red. "Ah… he wants to know if you have any food with you." 

Phainon had a half eaten roll of bread, so he gave it to the Pegasus. He looked around, wondering if the thief was nearby. Hyacine blinked. "Are you looking for anyone? You seemed to be running really fast earlier." 

"Right. About that…" Phainon rubbed the back of his head and explained what had happened. Hyacine's eyes widened. 

"Of course it's Cipher," she placed her hands on her waist. For such a small girl, her disappointed stare was really intimidating. "And you wanted to see Lady Aglaea? I was just heading to meet someone in that direction. I'll take you there!" 

"Really?" Phainon paused. "Ah, but about that execution…" 

Hyacine stomped her foot. "Lady Aglaea would never! Unless you were actually a traitor, of course. Come on, we can meet Cassie and I'll take you to see her." 

"Cassie" turned out to be another woman who was just about as purple as Hyacine was pink. She had a gentle smile, and smelled strongly of flowers. "It's a pleasure to meet you, Lord Phainon of Aedes Elysiae." 

Phainon blinked. Aedes Elysiae didn't have any lords, and even if they did, it sure wasn't going to be him. He extended his hand. "It's nice to meet you too, Lady Castorice!" 

Both Hyacine and Castorice stared at the hand like it was a ticking time bomb. Phainon slowly retracted it. 

People in Okhema sure were strange, weren't they? 

"Ah," Castorice said. She looked flustered and turned to Hyacine for help. 

Hyacine jumped in. "Sorry, Lord Phainon! We didn't make it clear. Cassie has been cursed since she was a child. Anyone who touches her dies." 

"Oh." Phainon was mortified. He'd met a grand total of two nice people in Okhema, and so far had ran over the pet of the first one and almost triggered the curse of the second. "My deepest apologies, Lady Castorice." 

"Please, just Castorice," she smiled softly at him. "Why are you seeking help from Lady Aglaea? Maybe we can be of assistance." 

Castorice and Hyacine had been nothing but nice to him, so it couldn't hurt to tell them the truth. "I'm looking for a star," he said. "Eurypon took him from me. But Mydei was mine first! I promised he wouldn't have to grant wishes if he didn't want to, and I broke that promise. I'm going to take him back home." 

"You're looking for a… star?" Castorice looked baffled. 

"Oh, Agy's mentioned it before, remember, Cassie?" Hyacine said. "When Castrum Kremnos first started attacking other regions, they said it was the work of the star." 

"It's not Mydei's fault!" Phainon snapped. "They have weapons that can hurt him! All he wanted to do was keep Aedes Elysiae safe." 

Hyacine and Castorice exchanged glances. "My apologies, Lord Phainon," Castorice said at last. "We will take you to Lady Aglaea. Her goals should align with yours." She hesitated. "By the way, this star—" 

"His name is Mydei." 

"Lord Mydei, then. Does he… have the ability to get rid of curses?" Castorice looked at him hopefully. Phainon bit his lip. So far, he had seen Mydei summon pieces of cake and gold. And whatever Eurypon made him do. But he didn't know if Mydei could cure something like this. Castorice's shoulders slumped. "Nevermind. Come. I will take you to Lady Aglaea." 

The moment Phainon stepped through the door to Aglaea's office, a flying projectile came straight toward him. He ducked, yelping. 

The person who had thrown it was an older man with long green hair and an eye patch. He was scowling at a blonde woman, most likely meaning to aim at her. "You— you— witch! You tricked me!" 

"I did not trick you," the lady, presumably Aglaea, said. 

"You told me that you had sensitive material related to my research!" 

Aglaea stared directly at Phainon. "And I do. He's right here. I've been waiting for you, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae." 

Yeah, no. Looks like Phainon was going to have to save Mydei by himself. He turned around and tried to open the door. It was locked. He whirled around to glare at Hyacine and Castorice, who stared back at him guiltily. 

"It's useless," the man snapped. "She's evil. She's not letting us go until she sucks our souls dry." 

"Phainon," Aglaea said patiently. "Why don't you explain to our dear Professor Anaxa why you are here today?" 

Phainon was too terrified to argue otherwise. He told Anaxa and Aglaea everything, from finding Mydei after the meteor shower, to inviting him to live with them, to how beautiful Mydei was, up to when Eurypon took him away. 

When he finished, Anaxa said, "So you've brought to me a lovesick boy who claims to have found a star. Not only that, but he lost said star and it is now the reason Castrum Kremnos is attacking everything with a pulse?" 

"Wait," Phainon cut in. "How did you even know about that, anyways?"

"Because of the prophecy," Anaxa mocked. "Honestly! If you're going to put all of your faith into some silly poems, might as well worship me instead!" 

The door flew open. "Agy!" a tiny redhead said. Wait no, three tiny redheads. "Naxy's being weird again! Tell him to stop!" They were dragging behind them another person. 

A very familiar person.

"You!" Phainon shouted. He pointed his finger. "That's the sword thief!" 

The woman sat up, spluttering. "I didn't steal anything! You gave it to me!" 

"I see you've met Cifera already," Aglaea said, at the same time one of the triplets demanded: "Ciphy! You've been stealing?" 

Phainon's head hurt so much. 

Eventually, everyone in the room settled down to get affairs in order. Phainon explained his predicament again, and Aglaea introduced everyone in the room. Anaxa ("It's Anaxagoras!") was a famous scholar from The Grove looking to pursue his research on souls. The triplets were Tribbie, Trianne, and Trinnon, and actually used to be one whole human. They were the ones to discover the prophecy relating to Phainon and the star. Cifera, aka Cipher, was a… thief. And Hyacine and Castorice seemed to be the only normal ones in the room, sans Castorice's touch of death and Hyacine's fat Pegasus.

"Look, I don't care about this prophecy," Phainon said impatiently. "All I want is to rescue Mydei. You can do whatever you want after. Speaking of — where's my sword?" 

"Aha, about that…" Cipher trailed off. "That sword wasn't going to get much done anyways! It barely sold enough to pay for my lunch!" 

Phainon's jaw dropped. It was the best sword in Aedes Elysiae! Though, considering Aedes Elysiae was a farming village and had never been under conflict before, that wasn't saying much. 

"There is no need for that," Aglaea cut in smoothly. "As a gesture of goodwill towards you, I will commission the finest sword and procure proper clothing that you can take with you on your journey." 

"How long will that take?" Phainon asked. "I don't want to keep Mydei waiting any longer." Two years had been long enough. 

"Lord Phainon, you shouldn't rush to save Lord Mydei no matter how much you care for him," Castorice warned. "Castrum Kremnos is a mobile war fortress, and even before the presence of the star, their warriors were formidable. Going in without a plan will only lead to death." 

"I've been trying to track down Castrum Kremnos," Cipher added irritably. "It could take us years to even infiltrate it." 

Years? But Phainon couldn't argue with what they were saying. Mydei would have to wait for him a bit longer.

"Which is why I propose for you to travel with a party," Aglaea said. "Unfortunately, I must remain in Okhema. But I would trust everyone here with my life. Except maybe Anaxa." 

"Fuck you too," Anaxa snapped back. He rolled his eyes. "I never believed in such foolish things like stars and wishes. But I am intrigued. Castrum Kremnos has some of the leading experts on soul research, and they've most likely been used on that star." 

Castrum Kremnos was experimenting about souls using Mydei? The room felt freezing cold all of a sudden. One of the triplets patted his leg. "It'll be okay!" she said. "De is strong, we can feel it." 

Hyacine said, "I would love to help you rescue Mydei! Every party needs a healer!" 

Castorice nodded. "I am by your side, Lord Phainon." 

Everyone turned to face Cipher, who made a face at them. "Fine! But I expect triple pay! For however long this takes!" 

And so, Phainon's adventure party started their first journey: Operation: Rescue Mydei! 

Three years passed by, and Phainon's adventure party had made significant progress on infiltrating Castrum Kremnos. Mydei still hadn't been seen since he was captured, but Phainon remained hopeful. Cyrene had kept him updated on Aedes Elysiae, and the barrier was still holding on. 

It flickers sometimes, she wrote. But it has continued keeping Aedes Elysiae safe. Don't worry about us, brother. How is your adventure party? 

Phainon had protested vehemently about the name of the traveling party. Why did it have to be Phainon's adventure party? Why couldn't it be anyone else? 

He wrote a long winded rant protesting how unfair it was that they were using his name. Then he tried to actually answer her question. Cipher kept stealing his stuff. Anaxa and Aglaea somehow hated each other more. Tribbie, Trinnon, and Trianne were as cute as ever. Little Ica got fatter. Castorice and Hyacine were still the most normal of the group, though they had their fair share of weird moments. 

In the end, Phainon wrote enough about his friends to fill a journal. He wanted Mydei to read about his journey when they were reunited. He also secretly hoped that Mydei would love them just as much as he did. 

There was motion outside of his tent. Hyacine poked her head inside, Castorice a safe distance behind her. "Phainon!" she said. "We have a surprise for you!" 

The group — this time including Aglaea and Anaxa for once — had been camping out by Castrum Kremnos's moving fortress. There were only a couple of days until Mydei's rescue. Phainon left the tent, wondering what the rest of his party was up to now. 

"HAPPY BIRTHDAY!" 

Everyone was gathered around the campfire, shouting at Phainon the moment he left the tent. The Tribios jumped up in down in joy, clapping their hands. "Snowy, Snowy! We made you a cake!" 

"Oh." For some reason, Phainon's eyes filled with tears. "You remembered?" Even though they'd done a celebration every year for his birthday, he hadn't expected them to do something this year. Not when the final battle was so close. 

"Of course, silly!" Hyacine said. "We would never forget! You mentioned how Mydei and Cyrene would always make you a cake but uhhh…" 

"It's my fault, Lord Phainon," Castorice sniffed. "I was in charge of making part of the cake batter." 

Aglaea took a sip of her tea. "The fault lies not with you, Castorice. Anaxa wanted to… experiment with some flavor combinations." 

"I didn't see you try to help fix the cake!" 

"Well, if we're all admitting what we did wrong," Cipher said. "I thought it would be funny to add some peppers to the cake. Good thing we didn't mix it properly!" 

Hyacine wailed out, "Little Ica ate all of the frosting!" Little Ica let out a small burp of satisfaction. 

The Tribios were holding the cake, looking up at him with their adorable wide eyes. The cake was quite possibly the ugliest thing Phainon had ever seen. 

He loved it. 

They had just gotten through the first bite of the cake when Hyacine sighed, forlorn. Even Little Ica didn't want their crumbs. 

"Damn," Cipher kicked a slice that had fallen to the ground. It was so hard, it bounced around until it eventually hit a tree. "This really makes me want to try one of Little Star's cakes." 

Phainon nonchalantly threw his slice into the fire. It lit up an angry red, as if the cake disgusted it that much. "His cakes were the best," he admitted. "We taught him how to make his own but he ended up baking the best out of all of us. On my fifteenth birthday, he made me the biggest cake ever." It had taken Cyrene and him months to finish it. They had missed Mydei too much. 

"That sounds nice," Castorice said. "Did he do anything else for you on your birthday?" She looked at him hopefully, trying to distract him from the cake. 

"We would go into the forest where we met," Phainon said, reminiscent. "And Mydei would summon me a piece of cake, even after I had finished the first one." 

Cipher slumped on the ground. "No fair! I want a star of my own!" 

Phainon joined her in sulking. "I miss Mydei," he grumbled. "He gave me a goodbye kiss before he was taken, and I didn't even get to give him one back." 

Anaxa whirled around mid-argument with Aglaea. "Wait a minute. The star kissed you?" 

"Uh, yeah," Phainon said, a bit surprised. 

"Like a kiss? On the lips?" 

Cipher muttered, "Aren't you a bit too old to be discussing your student's love life?" 

"You," Anaxa seethed, turning back on Aglaea. Phainon had no idea why he was so angry. "Does he know?" 

"No," Aglaea said. "And don't you dare tell him." 

The Tribios cheered. "Snowy's got a boy-friend!" 

The thought of Mydei being his boyfriend brought an instant smile to Phainon's face. He had wanted to court Mydei, but surely rescuing him was a better way to ask him out, right? 

His smile dropped. If they even managed to rescue Mydei at all. 

Perhaps sensing his bad mood, the rest of the heroes kept quiet for the rest of the night. It was only a few days before the final battle, after all. 

The final battle took place mere days after Phainon's birthday. There was no time to waste — the last bordering country had fell to Castrum Kremnos's onslaught, and Kephale's Dawn Device was failing. Phainon had been around Mydei's powers enough to know that it was his doing. But he also knew how strong Mydei was — if he wanted to, Kephale's Dawn Device would have already been destroyed. 

The battlefield was filled with a cacophony of bloodshed and fighting. Phainon rushed forward, eyes aimed on Castrum Kremnos's main palace. He only stopped to help those in need, before quickly moving on. 

Before the battle started, Aglaea had taken him aside for a private talk. I know that your priority is Mydei, she'd said. Do not worry about Okhema. As long as the star is safe, we will be fine. 

Phainon had nodded, but a part of him felt guilty. Lady Aglaea had taken care of him for the past five years, and he was practically abandoning her on the battlefield? 

But she was right. If he could retrieve Mydei, Eurypon couldn't use him to his advantage. 

"Snowy, here!" Tribbie gestured at him. "Ciphy and I found a way to the palace!" 

He snatched her arm. Tribbie closed her eyes, focused on opening a gate. The three dove into the gate, only to stagger back as a wave of arrows came down on them after they landed on the other wide. 

"Fuck!" Cipher hissed. Phainon moved to step in front of them when the sky lit up a brilliant gold, shielding them from the arrows. He gasped.

"Mydei?" 

There was no answer. Another flash of gold, and all of the archers collapsed. "They're sleeping," Cipher said, peering closer. "Your star's pretty powerful, huh?" 

It had been five years since Phainon had last seen Mydei. His blood tingled. He couldn't wait a minute longer. 

"Tribbie's out of it," Cipher nodded to the little girl, who was practically falling asleep standing up. "The shield will protect her, but I don't want to take any chances. I'll stay with her and cover you from behind." She stared at him. "Something tells me that you will be fine." 

"Cipher," Phainon breathed. They had come a long way from their first meeting. "Thank you. Really." 

She winked at him. "Just make sure to tell your star that you owe me a wish!" 

Phainon ran like his life depended on it. Which in a way, it really did. His path remained relatively clear — any stragglers he ran into were easily disposed of by either himself or Mydei's assistance. Eventually, he opened the door to a room. A large golden birdcage sat in the middle of it, and inside was — 

"Mydei!" 

Mydei looked up. His eyes widened. He had grown taller since they last saw each other, the top of his head almost hitting the cage. His hair was longer than ever, cascading down his back like a sunset-colored waterfall. His golden eyes remained the same, though. Still as stunning and piercing as Phainon last remembered them. 

"Phainon," the star breathed. He ran to the edge of the cage and gripped at the bars. Almost immediately, the metal began to burn away at his skin. "I thought I felt you, but I couldn't believe it. What are you doing here? Eurypon could come in at any second!" 

"I came for you," Phainon said. "No time to argue. I'm getting you out of here!" He swung at the cage with his sword. It didn't even dent. Anaxa had mentioned it was possible Eurypon had developed a type of metal strong enough to keep a star captive. Phainon couldn't understand how that was possible, but it seemed like Eurypon had managed it.

"It's no use," Mydei said. "The metal is indestructible. But Phainon. You have to listen to me. I need to tell you something." 

"Not now, Mydei!" Phainon gritted his teeth in concentration. Damn it. If only Cipher were here to try to pick the lock. Or maybe Little Ica could gnaw his way through the cage. 

The door flew open once more. King Eurypon stood there in all of his mad glory, dripping in blood. He smiled, feral, when he saw Phainon. "I remember you," he hissed. "You're that menace from Aedes Elysiae, wasn't it? How sweet that you've come for your lover. Too bad that by now you'll be the last survivor of your hometown. I've already sent my troops there." 

"You," Phainon snarled. He pointed his sword at Eurypon. "I'll kill you."

"Will you?" Eurypon asked. "And what will you do if I command your little star to kill you?" He turned towards Mydei, who glared at him. 

"I won't," Mydei grit out. The chains around him hissed and glowed bright red. He crumpled to his knees. "I refuse!" Golden blood dripped from his hairline. 

"How foolish," Eurypon said. "It seems my lessons haven't sunk in yet, even after all of this time. You would really give up everything for this boy? Even your soul?" 

Mydei moaned softly. "…Yes." 

Eurypon sighed, like he was disciplining his unruly son. "There's still use for you. It seems I will have to kill you after all, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae." He lifted his spear and lunged. 

Phainon had barely managed to block the first blow before Eurypon retaliated again, feinting towards the right. To his credit, he was clearly talented enough to lead an army of his own — he had done so for years before Mydei, after all. That, combined with whatever remaining strength he'd sapped from Mydei through his wishes, meant he was practically on another league of his own. 

But Phainon had also prepared for years for this. He wasn't about to lose to Eurypon after finally being able to see Mydei again. 

They met each other head on, equally matched. The battle must have lasted for hours before either side showed signs of tiring. Phainon didn't know what happened. Perhaps he had slipped up. Maybe Eurypon had just gotten lucky. But one thing led to another, and Phainon found himself being pushed onto his back, body covered in weeping wounds. Eurypon stalked towards him like a tiger about to attack a weak bunny. 

Phaionon looked up and locked eyes with Mydei's. If he were to die today, he wanted it to be with no regrets. "I love you," he whispered. "I wish you were free." 

Mydei froze. "Phainon," he said urgently. A broken cough wrenched its way out of his throat. Blood dribbled down his chin and landed to create a small puddle under him. "Phainon, answer me. Is that your wish?" 

Phainon wanted many things. He wanted to go back to Aedes Elysiae and play with Cyrene one more time. He wanted to listen to Aglaea and Anaxa argue again. He wanted to play hide and seek with the Tribios, to chase after Cipher when she stole something from him, to simply hang around with Hyacine and Castorice. But in all of his life, he knew that he only had one wish. 

"Yes," Phainon said instantly. "Even if I only had one wish, I would wish for you to be free." 

Mydei smiled at him. He reached through the bars and gently wiped the blood away from Phainon's face. "Then it is my duty as your star to grant your wish." 

The world lit up a brilliant gold, the same gold Phainon saw when Mydei had landed in Aedes Elysiae. 

When the light cleared, the cage laid shattered in pieces. Mydei stood there, free from any shackles. In his hands was a large spear, and a pair of six seraphim wings extended from his back. 

There you are, Phainon thought. There's my star. 

Eurypon stopped dead in his tracks. His eyes widened. "How…" 

Mydei lifted up his chin. "I gave my first kiss away to Phainon of Aedes Elysiae," he announced. "And by doing so, I gave him full control over my abilities. Your methods were only a cruel mimicry of getting me to submit, Eurypon. Your end is here." 

As it turned out, Mydei was even more beautiful in motion. He flowed like he was the only dancer on the stage, like the moon itself revolved around him. He was a star in a world filled with mortals. Phainon watched, enthralled. 

It took mere seconds for Eurypon to lose. Mydei didn't even wait for his cold body to hit the ground before he turned and ran to Phainon, lifting his head into his lap. He was so bright, it hurt to look at. Or was it that Phainon was having trouble seeing at all? All of a sudden, everything hurt. The wounds on his body seemed more deadly than they had just moments ago. 

Mydei gently stroked his cheek. "You fool," he chided. "Using all of your strength like that. I finally get to see you, and now you're on death's door." 

Phainon mumbled, "You're so beautiful, Mydei…" 

Mydei laughed. "I hope you love me just as much when I'm a human, Phainon. I would only ever do this for you." Before Phainon could ask him what he meant, Mydei leaned down and pressed their lips together once more. 

The change was instantaneous. Just like before, a surge of energy traveled throughout Phainon's body. He felt as though he could run a marathon. The scene shifted around him, and he saw stars again. Very familiar stars, all staring and huffing at him. 

Impossible. That's who little Mydeimos chose? This puny human? 

A star, giving up their divinity for love? Preposterous! 

Gorgo, you cannot possibly be okay with this! 

A bright crimson star in the middle of it all laughed. She had an oddly familiar, soothing voice. All of a sudden, Phainon felt his cheeks warm to an unbearably hot degree, like one of the stars had pinched them. 

He's sweet and kind. Handsome. He loves my son with all of his heart, enough to die for him. What more could a mother ask for? My son is happy. My heart is happy. 

The star shifted forms, transforming into a woman. She was the spitting image of Mydei. Her eyes crinkled when she looked at Phainon, and she leaned in to press a sweet kiss to his forehead. 

I give you my blessing, she said. May my son Mydeimos know that he is forever loved. 

Phainon opened his eyes. For a moment, he thought that he had died and the scene with the stars was an elaborate pre-afterlife dream. Then Little Ica backed up from his face and let out an annoyed doot doot. 

"Oh! Phainon, you're awake!" Hyacine waved at him happily. "How do you feel? Do you need anything?" 

Phainon's head was killing him. He gladly accepted the water. "What happened?" 

Hyacine explained everything to him. Once Mydei had killed Eurypon, the effects of all of his wishes had disappeared. Weapons and armor vanished on the battlefield, previously indisposed warriors were able to fight again, and Castrum Kremnos's army was eventually driven out. Aglaea and Castorice had stormed the palace and found an unconscious Phainon and Mydei, and took them to the hospital wing. 

Phainon had a sneaking suspicion that what triggered the reversal of the wishes wasn't Eurypon's death at all. He glanced to the side of the bed where Mydei was sleeping peacefully, arms tucked under his head. "Sorry, Hyacine," he said. "Do you mind giving us some time alone?" 

The second she left, Mydei lifted his head. "You knew I was awake all along." 

Instead of saying something stupid like: I know all of your habits, even after five years apart, Phainon did the next best thing and crashed their lips together. Mydei melted the moment they came into contact, practically seeping into his arms. Phainon shifted to easily allow Mydei to rest on top of his chest. When they finally separated, Mydei's cheeks and lips were bright red. "What was that for?" 

Phainon licked his lips. "I just wanted to initiate a kiss for once," he said honestly. He lifted his thumb to trace Mydei's cheekbone. "You're not a star anymore," he murmured. 

"No," Mydei said. "I gave that up. Saving you was more important." He smirked. "Your friend Cipher was upset when she heard. She wanted the ability to turn into a cat. Just what have you been up to while I was gone?" 

Phainon ignored him. "You're not mad though?" he asked. "Even if it means never traveling the skies again?" 

"I have you," Mydei said simply. "I've spent most of my life living as a human, and then as a star. I prefer being a human more." 

Phainon buried his face in Mydei's neck, overwhelmed. "I think I met your mother." His voice was muffled. "She says she loves you. And that we have her blessing." 

"Mama did? Of course, what am I saying. She probably knew all along." Mydei smiled for the first time since they were in the hospital. "I love you," he whispered, like he was telling Phainon a secret. 

Phainon smiled. He thought of little ten year old Phainon, watching the meteor showers for the first time, delighted. He remembered falling in love the moment he laid his eyes on Mydei. He wondered if both children would be proud of the choices they'd made today. 

Of course they would. There wasn't a universe where Phainon didn't fall in love with Mydeimos. 

Phainon lifted Mydei's braid to press a kiss to it. "And I love you, my Little Star," he breathed out. He felt impossibly warm, like he was being embraced by the sun itself. 

I wish that Mydeimos will forever know that he is loved.
